nodes.description: CV and OER activity of pure NiOOH films in Fe-free 0.1 M MOH solutions

Ni_II_to_Ni_III_shift.value: no modification for Li+, Na+, K+; moderate shift for TBA+, TMA+

OER_activity.value: nearly identical for K+ and TMA+

nodes.source_text: The oxidation behavior of the electrodeposited nickel oxyhydroxide films was studied by cyclic voltammetry in Fe-free 0.1 M MOH solution... No modification of the NiII to NiIII oxidation potential is observed for Li+, Na+, and K+, while a moderate shift towards greater potential is observed for TBA+ and TMA+. ... it is found to be nearly identical for pure NiOOH when using K+ and TMA+. The Tafel slope is also found to be identical and equal to circa 60 mV/decade

nodes.description: CV and OER activity of Fe-containing Ni(Fe)OOH films in 0.1 M MOH solutions
nodes.source_text: For Fe-containing films, the Ni3+/Ni2+ redox peak is largely influenced by the nature of the cation, and a shift towards greater potential as large as 78 mV was measured between K+ and TMA+... the OER activity for Ni(Fe)OOH films decreases between alkaline cations (K+ and Na+) and TMA+. Moreover, a change in the Tafel slope from 35 mV/decade to 55 mV/decade

nodes.description: OER pH dependence above pH 12 for K+ and TMA+
nodes.source_text: For a pH value above about 12, the OER activity as well as the Tafel slopes remain constant for both cations (Tafel slopes of approx. 30 mV/decade for K+ and approx. 60 mV/decade for TMA+). Moreover, above pH 12, (∂E/∂pH)i = 0 giving a rate order for H+ of 0 on the RHE scale

nodes.description: OER activity pH dependence below pH 12
nodes.source_text: Below this pH value, the OER activity decreases and the Tafel slope is found to increase up to a value close to 90 mV/decade for TMA+ and 60 mV/decade for K+

nodes.description: OER in H2O vs D2O solutions

OER_activity.value: no modification from H2O to D2O

nodes.source_text: For Fe-free films, switching from proton to deuterium does not modify the OER activity (Figure 3)

nodes.description: Isotopic effect on OER activity in 0.1 M KOH H2O vs D2O
nodes.source_text: However, for Fe-containing films, the use of deuterated water significantly decreases the OER activity in KOH solution. Not only the OER activity decreases, but also the Tafel slope increases when using deuterated water

nodes.description: Isotopic effect on OER activity in 0.1 M TMAOH H2O vs D2O

isotopic_effect.value: PCET mechanism presumably independent of TMA+

nodes.source_text: Bearing in mind that a PCET mechanism is presumably at play independently of the use of TMA+, the isotopic effect indicates that hydrogen bonds network must be influencing the OER kinetics

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows no modification of Ni(II)/Ni(III) oxidation potential for Li+, Na+, K+; moderate shift for TBA+, TMA+ in pure NiOOH; 78 mV shift between K+ and TMA+ in Fe-containing Ni(Fe)OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No modification of the NiII to NiIII oxidation potential is observed for Li+, Na+, and K+, while a moderate shift towards greater potential is observed for TBA+ and TMA+. For Fe-containing films... a shift towards greater potential as large as 78 mV was measured between K+ and TMA+.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ UV/Vis shows 10% transmission loss correlated to Ni2+ to Ni3+ oxidation and deprotonation for KOH, TMAOH, Fe-containing KOH; lower loss for Fe-containing TMAOH indicating specific TMA+ interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similar electrochromic behaviors were found for purified KOH and TMAOH as well as for Fe-containing KOH solutions, with a clear decrease of the transmission correlated to the oxidation of Ni2+ to Ni3+... while the transmission loss reaches 10% for these solutions, this value is lower when measured in Fe-containing TMAOH solution.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy visualizes different oxygen species formed depending on deprotonation process, showing specific interaction with TMA+ cation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Hence, depending on the deprotonation process, different oxygen species are formed on the surface of the films that show, or not, specific interaction with TMA+ cation, as visualize by Raman spectroscopy.
